The \wikilink{s41--b009}{bound for a simple extension} and
\wikilink{s41--b011}{primitive element theorem} give a useful immediate
bound for number fields.

\begin{corollary}\label{number-field-bound}
If $[K:\mathbb Q]=n<\infty$, then $K$ has at most $2^n$ subfields.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}\label{number-field-bound-proof}
Characteristic zero makes the extension separable, hence simple by
the primitive element theorem. The existing simple-extension bound
applies. Every subfield contains the prime field $\mathbb Q$, so its
subfields are exactly its intermediate fields over $\mathbb Q$.
\end{proof}
\begin{remark}\label{number-field-bound-method}
The bound uses minimal polynomials over intermediate fields, not an
estimate for the degree of a normal closure. It is an upper bound,
not a claim that all subsets of the roots produce intermediate fields.
\end{remark}
